title: Frosted glass with backdrop-filter
summary: backdrop-filter blurs whatever is behind a translucent panel; filter blurs the element itself.
explanation: filter changes the element and its content. backdrop-filter changes what can be seen through the element: here a blur of the colourful shapes behind the panel. The panel needs a see-through background (rgb with an alpha), or there is nothing to see through.
A thin, semi-transparent white border and a soft shadow sell the glass edge. The panel is positioned over the shapes so they overlap.
Blur is expensive for the browser to draw, so use it on a few panels, not on a long scrolling list.
tryThis: Change blur(12px) to blur(2px) and then to blur(30px).
Make the background fully opaque (rgb(255 255 255 / 1)): the blur is hidden behind it.
Replace backdrop-filter with filter: blur(12px): now the panel's own text is blurred.

children.text: The shapes behind are blurred, not the text.
